name: Question 17
problem: Find the principal axes of the curve $24{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+21{x}_{2}^{2}=100.$
worked_solution:
First, consider the quadratic form $Q(x)=24{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+21{x}_{2}^{2}.$ The matrix of the form is 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}24 & 2 \\ 2 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that $A$ is symmetric. The principal axes of the curve 

$$
{x}^{T}\,Ax=100
$$

are the vectors that form an orthonormal eigenvector basis of $A.$ 

By solving the characteristic equation $|A-\lambda I|=0,$ we obtain

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=25\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{2}=20.$

Let's now find the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=25,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-25I & =[\begin{aligned}24 & 2 \\ 2 & 21\end{aligned}]-25[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-25I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{1}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{1}‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=20,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-20I & =[\begin{aligned}24 & 2 \\ 2 & 21\end{aligned}]-20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-20I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

$\,$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Question 17

Find the principal axes of the curve 24x12+4x1x2+21x22=100.

a
110[31] and 110[−13]
b
12[11] and 12[−11]
c
113[23] and 113[−32]
d
15[21] and 15[−12]
e
13[11] and 13[−11]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, consider the quadratic form Q(x)=24x12+4x1x2+21x22. The matrix of the form is

A=[242221].

Notice that A is symmetric. The principal axes of the curve

xTAx=100

are the vectors that form an orthonormal eigenvector basis of A.

By solving the characteristic equation |A−λI|=0, we obtain

λ1=25 and λ2=20.

Let's now find the eigenvectors.

  • For λ1=25, we have A−25I=[242221]−25[1001]=[−122−4]. Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−25I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v1=[21]. Dividing v1 by its norm ‖v1‖=5, we get v1‖v1‖=15[21].

  • For λ2=20, we have A−20I=[242221]−20[1001]=[4221]. Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−20I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v2=[−12]. Dividing v2 by its norm ‖v2‖=5, we get v2‖v2‖=15[−12].

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

15[21] and 15[−12].
